sections.title: Pre-hospital fibrinolysis
sections.recommendation: If trained medical or allied health staff can interpret the ECG on site or transmit the ECG for remote interpretation, initiate fibrinolytic therapy in the pre-hospital setting. Use a fibrin-specific agent (tenecteplase, alteplase, or reteplase) with the goal of starting fibrinolytic therapy within 10 minutes of STEMI diagnosis. Do not delay initiation for cardiac biomarker results.
key_points: Preferred fibrin-specific agents: tenecteplase, alteplase, reteplase.
Goal: start fibrinolysis within 10 minutes of STEMI diagnosis.
Do not wait for cardiac biomarker testing before starting fibrinolysis.
evidence: Meta-analysis of six randomized trials (n = 6434) showed pre-hospital fibrinolysis reduced early mortality by 17%, particularly when administered in the first 2 hours after symptom onset.

STREAM trial: pre-hospital fibrinolysis followed by early PCI had similar outcomes to transfer for PPCI in STEMI patients presenting within 3 hours who could not undergo PPCI within 1 hour of first medical contact; slight excess of intracranial bleeding observed, which was reduced by halving the dose of tenecteplase in patients >75 years.

sections.title: Angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention after fibrinolysis (pharmaco-invasive strategy)
sections.recommendation: Transfer patients to a PCI centre immediately after initiation of lytic therapy. In cases of failed fibrinolysis or evidence of re-occlusion/re-infarction with recurrent ST-segment elevation, immediate angiography and rescue PCI are indicated. Routine early angiography (within ~2–24 hours) after fibrinolysis is recommended even if initial reperfusion appears successful.
key_points: Immediate transfer to PCI centre after initiation of lytic therapy is recommended.
Failed fibrinolysis, re-occlusion or recurrent ST-elevation: immediate angiography and rescue PCI.
Re-administration of fibrinolysis is not beneficial and is discouraged.
Routine early angiography (within 2–24 h) after fibrinolysis reduces rates of reinfarction and recurrent ischemia versus a 'watchful waiting' strategy.
evidence: Several randomized trials showed routine early angiography with subsequent PCI reduced re-infarction and recurrent ischaemia compared with watchful waiting.

Network meta-analysis including 15,357 STEMI patients compared fibrinolytic therapy (n = 4212), PPCI (n = 6139), and fibrinolysis followed by routine immediate or early PCI (n = 5006) to investigate transfer to PCI-capable facilities.

Pharmaco-invasive approach (transfer within a day, e.g. <24 h) was the second most favourable approach after PPCI; reported OR for death 0.79 (95% CI 0.59–1.08) compared with conventional fibrinolytic strategy.

clinical_endpoints_and_thresholds: ST-segment resolution >50% at 60–90 minutes is mentioned as an indicator of successful reperfusion.
Early mortality reduction (17%) with pre-hospital fibrinolysis in meta-analysis.

Timing thresholds: fibrinolysis within 2 hours of symptom onset associated with greater benefit; presentation within 3 hours relevant for strategy decisions; aim to start fibrinolysis within 10 minutes of diagnosis; transfer/PPCI within 1 hour of first medical contact when possible; pharmaco-invasive transfer within <24 h.
special_considerations: Slight excess of intracranial bleeding observed with pre-hospital investigational strategy; reduced by halving tenecteplase dose in patients >75 years.
Re-administration of fibrinolysis in the same setting is discouraged.
